acceptanceCriteria: `.golangci.yaml` with the standard preset plus misspell exists, every exclusion carries a reason, and a `golangci-lint-check` GATE_STEPS entry runs it with a pinned tool version.
A `shellcheck-check` GATE_STEPS entry covers `script/*.sh` with a pinned tool version.
`make gate` passes on the commit that introduces both steps, either clean or against a recorded ratchet count that a later run may only lower.
body:
Filed on 2026-09-22 from a review of https://github.com/agent-substrate/substrate (head d277088, 2026-09-22).

The Corvint gate runs `go vet`, `cross-vet` and `check-go-format`, and nothing else over Go or shell source: no staticcheck, no misspell, no shellcheck. Nine scripts under `script/` carry `# shellcheck disable=` comments as if a shellcheck gate existed, but none is wired into `GATE_STEPS` or `.github/workflows/`.

Substrate's `.golangci.yaml` is a reasonable starting template: golangci-lint v2 `default: standard` (errcheck, govet, ineffassign, staticcheck, unused) plus `misspell` with `locale: US`, every exclusion carrying a one-line reason, QF quickfix rules suppressed, generated paths excluded, `errcheck` off in `_test.go`. `hack/verify/shellcheck.sh` and `hack/verify/golangci-lint.sh` are each one short script.

Caveat: the first run will surface a backlog across a codebase this size. Scope the ticket as: add the config and the two GATE_STEPS entries, pin the tool version the way `check-host-package-versions` pins others, and either clean the findings or record a ratchet count the way `script/diagnostic-coverage.count` does, so the gate is green on the first commit and only forbids regression. The tool must be an offline, pinned binary; the default local product cannot grow a network dependency (invariant 7).
title: gate: standard-preset golangci-lint and shellcheck steps
